PROTAC-DB 4.0: an expanded knowledgebase of targeted protein degradation modalities with AI-powered knowledge discovery.

PROTAC-DB 4.0 is an updated knowledgebase that expands beyond classical PROTACs to include molecular glues and XTACs, covering the growing landscape of targeted protein degradation modalities. The resource aims to keep pace with rapid growth in TPD technologies and AI-driven drug discovery.

Persistent atrial fibrillation in older adults: Comparison of seven models and development of a gradient boosting machine classifier in a single-center observational study.

This single-center observational study of 572 older adults compared seven classification models for identifying persistent atrial fibrillation and selected a gradient boosting machine (GBM) classifier as the best performer. The work also examined clinical correlates of persistent AF and interpreted the chosen GBM model to understand which features drove its predictions.

Computational Discovery of Plant-Derived Peptides with Therapeutic Potential: A Scoping Review.

This scoping review maps the literature on computational discovery of plant-derived peptides with therapeutic potential, screening over 5,000 records and charting 79 sources published between 2021 and 2026. Species phylogenetics using intraprotein residue dependence inferred with protein foundation models.

This preprint proposes using protein foundation models to infer phylogenetic relationships from patterns of dependence between residues within proteins, rather than relying on traditional alignment-based substitution models that assume site independence. It distinguishes between single-sequence models (ESM) that yield residue attention matrices and MSA-based models (MSA Transformer) that yield sequence attention matrices, using these learned dependence signals as phylogenetic characters. The approach offers a potential alternative route to species phylogenetics that captures intraprotein epistatic information typically ignored by standard methods.

Viral host assignment across the tree of life with VHAMSTeR.

LongVerse: verified AI agents for Nanopore and PacBio DNA methylation analysis.

LongVerse is a system that converts a single English sentence into haplotype-resolved DNA methylation calls from Nanopore or PacBio reads, using AI agents that configure a pinned pipeline rather than writing code. On the HG002 reference genome, the agent's output was byte-identical to a human expert's (r = 1.000) and agreed well with bisulfite sequencing (r = 0.943 and 0.884), at a cost of $0.12–$0.54 per run. The work demonstrates that agent outputs can be validated against an independent measurement rather than only rubrics or LLM judges.

Estimating rates of SARS-CoV-2 lineage spread using graph spectra from genetic sequence data.

This offers a scalable way to prioritize sequences of concern amid massive genomic surveillance streams.

The findings suggest that general protein language models offer no clear advantage over simple sequence comparison for this task, highlighting the importance of germline-aware or receptor-specific modeling.
